answer: Sybil resistance bonds each identity in a collateral escrow and makes coordinated equivocation costly: if k identities equivocate on the same conflicting messages, the slashing penalty scales as O(k²), rather than linearly. Upon detection, controlling a swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss, so dividing stake among identities magnifies the operator’s downside. The names willow, opal, and violet confer no special status; only bonded collateral and verifiable behavior matter.
